body:
This PR add a FAQ entry we can use to point users to when they propose to extend existing UI elements or add new fancy features to Click.

The Tl;Dr is: we keep maintaining the existing stuff, don't add funky widgets, and aligns with Python upstream direction.

title: Add `context_settings` parameter to `CliRunner.invoke`

labels.name: docs
labels.description: Updates to documentation, readme, docstrings, typos

labels.name: test runner
labels.description: CliRunner and Click's test utilities feature

body:
This PR adds a `context_settings` parameter to `CliRunner.invoke()`, allowing tests to pass context-specific settings to the command's `Context`.

`CliRunner.invoke()` passes its extra keyword arguments to the `Context` of the command, except `color`: its own `color` parameter takes that name. `context_settings` solves this collision. And now a test can set what its terminal supports, as well as the `color` of the context in the same call.

With this addition, I can now test cases that were previously difficult or impossible to cover, such as verifying how the command behaves with different `Context` settings.

This was proposed 5 years ago in #2110 but at that time this change was evaluated as niche. Since then, we did a lot of color handling improvements in Click (#3505, #3653, #3739) which added a lot of color-related tests, so this is no longer a niche concern.

For evidence, I used the new `context_settings` parameter to extend and simplify existing checks. See `test_prompt_and_confirm_ansi_respects_color` and `test_tempfile_pager_handles_ansi`.

title: use the path_type to perform the other click.Path checks
body:
click.Path exposes a path_type but does currently not use it for path sanity checks such as exists, file_okay, dir_okay etc.
If path_type is for instance a cloudpathlib.AnyPath and the cli user points to a S3 those checks will always go wrong since they expect path_type to handle only local paths.
Issue #2661 addressed similar thoughts but when the path_type itself is pathlib compliant, I would hope that click.Path would honor the users wish to supply their own path_type.

title: Prevent Click from terminating when less is interrupted

labels.name: docs
labels.description: Updates to documentation, readme, docstrings, typos

body:
Today, if I stream output to `less` from Click, I can enter follow mode (`F`):
> ```
>        F      Scroll  forward,  and  keep  trying to read when the end of file is reached.  Normally this command would be used when already at the end of the file.  It is a way to monitor the
>               tail of a file which is growing while it is being viewed.  (The behavior is similar to the "tail -f" command.)  To stop waiting for more data, enter the interrupt character (usu‐
>               ally ^C).  On some systems you can also use ^X.
> ```

As described, SIGINT is used to exit that mode... That kills Click, though (i.e. no more output is produced)!
This behavior appears to be intentional, but there does not appear to be a way to have output continue.
If we were to suppress background interrupts, I could still get Click to terminate by exiting the pager.

Is this something the project would entertain (i.e. adding SIGINT isolation during paging), perhaps behind a flag if both behaviors are desirable?

title: Split `PAGER` and `EDITOR` with a Windows-specific `shlex` equivalent
body:
When I implemented https://github.com/pallets/click/pull/3777 a couple of weeks ago, I was annoyed by Windows behavior. And wondered why `shlex.split` is only available on Unix-like platforms. Then while cleaning ancient Python 2 stuff in https://github.com/pallets/click/pull/3817/changes#diff-3bd2075eb8cab59a601f5a021078e5763eea117ae315b04d8d2d719de1f45a97R48 , I discovered `CommandLineToArgvW`.

This is an attempt to rely on `CommandLineToArgvW`, which seems to do the trick, as a Windows equivalent to [`shlex.split`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/shlex.html#shlex.split).

But digging deeper I stumbled upon the discussion upstream at https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/44990#issuecomment-2084965003 , which explain why it was not considered for inclusion in the Python stdlib:

> on Windows, there isn't a single "shell syntax" to target - PowerShell and CMD have very different quoting rules, etc, and the fact that commands can do their own command line parsing (they get passed a command line string rather than an argument array) adds even more complexity.

And that explain why this PRs has limits, and why I choose to keep the shell completion relying on `shlex`.

I propose this PR anyway as it seems to bring the behavior more in line with Windows default, but kept as draft as I need a bit of feedback about this attempt.

### Tests

I collected test cases from past discussions to build up a more comprehensive suite:
- #1760
- #1477
- #2486

title: Print `\x04` and `\x1a` input bytes as `^D` and `^Z` in `CliRunner`

labels.name: test runner
labels.description: CliRunner and Click's test utilities feature

body:
This PR change `CliRunner` to translate the control bytes and render them differently on output:

| `<stdin>` byte | Echoed to `<stdout>` as | Pressed keys             |
|----------------|-------------------------|--------------------------|
| `\x04`         | `^D\n`                  | `Ctrl+D` on Unix    |
| `\x1a`         | `^Z\n`                  | `Ctrl+Z` on Windows |

It also no longer passes these bytes to the command.

As this introduce behavioral changes, it targets 8.6.0.

This will remove an hard-coded patch in `pallets-sphinx-themes` and a follow-up PR is maintained at https://github.com/pallets/pallets-sphinx-themes/pull/133 so you can see the benefits of this change.
